segments.text: In this town, nobody can lie. Except me.
If you try, the truth just comes out. Ask a waiter how the fish is, and he'll tell you it's three days old.
I found out when I was eight. My mom asked who broke the window. I pointed at my brother, and everyone believed me.
From that day on, I lied about everything. I never did my homework. I never lost a game.
And by the time I grew up, I was the richest man in town. Not because I was smart, but because I was the only one who could say: trust me.
Then I met Lily. She was the only person I never wanted to lie to.
One night, I asked her: do you love me? She said yes. And in this town, that meant it was true.
On our wedding day, right before the kiss, Lily leaned in and whispered:
You know... I can lie too.
Twenty years later, I still don't know if she meant it. Or if that was the lie.
Would you want to be the only one who can lie?
